08b.name: The Great Journey
08b.note: Tartarus is a SCRIPTED fight. From H2EK's own 08b_deltacontrol_boss.hsc:  • He is ai_cannot_die, and each phase ends when his body vitality is PINNED, not when he dies (2 phases on Normal, 3 Heroic, 4 Legendary).  • The script calls unit_set_maximum_vitality on him at the start of every phase (300 Normal / 350 Heroic / 400 Legendary), so his Body Vitality and Shield Vitality cards are overwritten and do nothing here.  • The damage window opens only once his shield is chipped below 0.975 (Normal), 0.95 (Heroic) or 0.9 (Legendary), and then lasts just 2-3s (1-3s Heroic, 1-2s Legendary) before the script closes it again.  • JOHNSON'S BEAM IS REAL DAMAGE. unit_impervious is cleared on Tartarus once the fight starts and he only takes damage from the player's TEAM, which Johnson is on (ai_allegiance player human). The script tops his shield back to full immediately before each of Johnson's volleys so the break reads cleanly, then Johnson's 3-round burst chews it down. Johnson fires every 4-10s on Normal. This is why the speedrun tech is to duplicate Johnson — more beam damage per volley crosses the threshold sooner. Options has an 'Extra Johnsons (08b)' setting to try it.  • Elite reinforcements respawn on a 30-60s timer whenever 3 or fewer are alive.  So what makes this fight winnable again: extra Johnsons, your own weapon damage, and Tartarus's Gravity Hammer and AI cards — those are real tags and are not script-overridden. His vitality cards are not.

Player Health.desc: The player's actual health pool — 75 in Halo 1, 30 in Halo 2, 45 in Halo 3, 80 in ODST. This is the pool itself, on the player's model; Starting Health Modifier only scales what you spawn with.

Shield Recharge.desc: How long the General's shield waits before recharging, and how long it takes.

Grenade Chance.desc: How readily the Zealot throws grenades. Depends on the pending value insertion: this variant inherits the block from its parent, so the card does nothing until its own copy exists.

Body Vitality.desc: The named Zealot's health (stock: 110 Normal, 150 Legendary). The Pillar of Autumn only — see the card note.

Shield Vitality.desc: The named Zealot's shield (stock: 185 Normal, 285 Legendary). The Pillar of Autumn only — see the card note.

Melee Behavior.desc: How often the Zealot commits to a melee lunge, and how far it reaches. Only the named Zealot defines these; the plain story Elites inherit them.

Body Vitality.desc: The Ultra's health (stock: 60 Normal, 90 Legendary — double an ordinary Grunt).

Shield Vitality.desc: The Ultra's shield (stock: 50 at every difficulty — Reach's only shielded Grunt).

Grenade Chance.desc: How readily the Ultra throws grenades (stock: 0.1).

Body Vitality.desc: The sniper Jackal's health (stock: 60 Normal, 90 Legendary — triple an ordinary Jackal, and it carries no shield gauntlet).

Body Recharge.desc: How fast the sniper Jackal heals between shots.

Eyepatch.desc: No aim assist. Every weapon loses its autoaim and magnetism — the reticule stops sticking and your aim stops bending onto targets.

Betrayal.desc: Every human squad turns on you. Marinel join the Flood in Halo 1 and the Heretics in Halo 2 and 3, so the Covenant keeps fighting them too.
